SUPER MARIO Boo's Mansion Kids Halloween Hide-and-Seek Game with 10 Figurines and Accessories We had so much fun with this. While we did not do the whole party element with people watching us unbox, we had a great time just on a normal day when the kids had done a great job, having a special treat of opening up each of the flaps to see what was inside.

A glow-in-the-dark boo, another boo, both with movable arms, a skeleton for around the plant and a dry bones were the highlights for us in this set. The Princess peach, also was detailed to an extent I have never seen on any of our other Princess peach figures. Usually they just fill in and under her skirt with solid plastic, and this one they gave her legs, undershorts, and high-heeled shoes underneath her dress so it is much more of a realistic figure than usual. I think either Mario or Luigi, needed a little plastic stand to be able to stand up and not just topple over. I would've appreciated a little more design on those guys so that they could be played with without an additional little clear plastic stand.

The flap opening and unveiling of the characters was a lot of fun. The characters were almost impossible in some cases to get out of the container without completely destroying the entire packaging, so my kids had to be flexible to wait until we were done opening all the flaps, then tear open the packaging to be able to push from the back and get some of those characters out. However, they were definitely firmly and securely packaged in there and were not going anywhere or getting damaged with those vacuum formed spots to sit.

Overall this was a lot of fun, and with the excellent quality of the figures, made for a very special and memorable gifting event to the kids.

text_fidelity_a:
Kelsyus Premium Floating Lounger XL with Fast Inflation, Inflatable Recliner Chair, Lake & Pool Float for Adults with Cup Holder, Amazon Exclusive First the good.
I shot light rapids in this puppy on the Blackfoot River in Montana. The collapsibility makes it easy to bring even if you don't have a pickup truck. You could put several in a compact car. You can blow it up with your own lungs in under five minutes, easily. It has good back support, very comfortable. The nylon cover protects from rocks. The foot rest and low profile give unparalleled maneuverability in rapids. You can get your arms deeper into the water than a traditional tube and the brace your feet on the foot rest to keep your seat when the ride gets wild. The handles allow you to stay in when it gets hectic. I got dumped once and because I was holding the handles, I was able to spin in a downhill rapid and shove it underwater and back under my tuchas to regain my seat.
It has all the advantages of an innertube and a kayak with the comfort of a recliner. The cup holder is also handy.
The bad:
The mesh is flimsy. All they need to do is use the stuff that more common blue and white float tubes use and they have a far better product. I got two small holes going over rocks. That doesn't happen with the blue and white tubes.
Fortunately, I can sew. I'm going to get some better mesh and pimp my floaty!
text_fidelity_b: Kelsyus Premium Floating Lounger XL with Fast Inflation, Inflatable Recliner Chair, Lake & Pool Float for Adults with Cup Holder, Amazon Exclusive

There are 7 numbered bags and 2 additional bags for the slides, large plates, and the monorail tracks. There is 1 sticker sheet with over 20 stickers.

This set is aimed towards girls 7-12. Instead of normal Lego minifigs, there are four mini-doll figures. Once finished, the resort has plenty of play details, with the monorail, slides, and various shops. This set isn’t overly sturdy; if you want to move it after construction, I recommend having an adult do it. The monorail track fell off when I tried to move mine. Easy enough to fix, but it might be disappointing for kids to see.

Perhaps my expectations (and preferences) are high, considering I normally construct Star Wars, Harry Potter, Ideas, and Architecture sets. I didn’t find Heartlake City Resort a particularly enjoyable build. It’s easy and repetitive. If I were to buy a set for a gift, I’d want it to demonstrate different building techniques or at least be fun to construct.

I also didn’t like the large number of stickers. In some sets, you can skip applying the stickers and not lose appeal, but I think they’re necessary here, especially to add some pizzazz to all the white.

text_fidelity_a:
dreambuilderToy Building Bricks 1100 Pieces Set with All Popular Building Blocks The theme for my five-year old's birthday party was Lego Batman. Therefore, I needed a bunch of Lego bricks to make decorations, but I did not want to pay an expensive Lego price and I also just needed basic bricks and colors. Enter the Dreambuilder Toy Building Bricks with 1000 bricks! Not only did I get exactly what I wanted, but I also got a superior toy. I was able to "build" all the decorations I needed (a napkin and silverware holder) with lots of bricks to spare, but when the party was over, I gave my son all the bricks and he was none the wiser that these were not "real" Legos. Some of the older boys at the party inspected the decorations and were able to come to a conclusion that these were in fact not real Legos, but that does not matter because they function exactly like real Legos.

Within the bag you get basic bricks in various sizes, 1x1, 2x2, 2x6, 2x8, etc. There is also one small, green building plate. The set also comes with various bricks for roofs, doors, fences, and windows. The colors are Roy G. Biv with black, white, and grey added. There are equal amounts of each color. We do have a real Lego 1000 piece "creative" bucket and here are the differences. There is no idea booklet with this. However, I do believe you can check their website for building ideas. Therefore, if free form building is not for your child like it is for mine, then this set is not for you. There is no brick separator, and the really flat bricks that drove us adults insane when we were kids are back to haunt to us. You will need to purchase one separately unlike the Lego creative sets. The Lego creative sets have more unique bricks, which take away from having more basic bricks to build bigger and better things as you would with this set. Dreambuilder bricks do not come with a storage bucket. You will receive a plastic bag with all of the bricks contained within that bag. So, you will need your own storage box.

Overall, I find the Dreambuilder bricks to be vastly superior to Lego if you are into simple, old school, free building without instructions. I will be purchasing additional sets.
text_fidelity_b: dreambuilderToy Building Bricks 1100 Pieces Set with All Popular Building Blocks

CALOVER Gift Toys for Kids Cat Dog Remote Control Mock Rat Mouse Mice Prank Gag Funny Practical Joke Toy for Holiday Party Late last year, for a week or so, all 3 of our cats sat gathered around the stove in the kitchen just staring at it. I quickly figured that was probably NOT a good sign-that we likely had an uninvited guest in our home. A few days later, I was proven correct. Got up early one morning to take the dog out and there was a dead mouse by the front door waiting to greet me, with 2 of the 3 cats sitting close by, proud of what they had left for me. (I don't think I've ever screamed louder in my entire life than I did that morning! lolol-I did heap praise on them after I calmed down) Unfortunately, the cats were once again gathered around the stove watching...and a few days later, mouse #2 was waiting for us to clean up. (Thank God I didn't find that one)

As soon as I saw this cat toy, I immediately ordered it. Though one of our 3 cats who helped catch the mice has since gone to the Rainbow Bridge, I knew the other 2, Miss Piggy and Squeaky, would have loads of fun playing with this toy. (And if I'm being honest, I want to keep them in tip-top shape in case any further 'uninvited guests' find their way into our home! lol) The mouse (I see it more of a rat than a mouse) is nearly 11 inches long from the tip of the nose to the end of the tail. It has beady red eyes that light up. From a distance, I believe people (who don't know its fake) could mistaken it for a real mouse (rat). It has gray fur and what appears to be sharp teeth sticking out of its mouth. (The teeth are NOT sharp, they only appear that way) The mouse takes 3 AAA batteries (not included) and the remote controller takes 2 AAA batteries as well. (not included) The only assembly required is placing the batteries in the mouse and controller. A nice, small screwdriver comes with the toy, something I especially appreciate! (Works on my eyeglass hinges as well!) The controller allows you to move the mouse forward and backward. (Both of our young kids were able to operate the remote control without issue while we stood with them) It does work on carpet but works far better on flooring. As soon as we turned it on and began steering it around the room, 2 cats immediately popped out of their beds, their curiosity piqued. Both cats watched the mouse zip around the floor for a bit. As soon as it got close to Miss Piggy, she jumped and ran under the bed. lol. But Squeaky...he was far braver than Piggy and watched it up close. We'd stop it for awhile and he'd creep closer and closer to it, staring at it....and then we'd start it up again. lol. It was loads of fun to watch him with this toy. It certainly kept him entertained for quite some time! Piggy stayed hidden but she's a nosy cat...she'll get the hang of it before long.

This is a fun toy not only for cats but for cat owners to operate for their cats! We had loads of fun watching the cat's reaction. Its a great way for your cat to get some exercise as well. Very easy to operate also!

UPDATE******************

We got this out again tonight to play with. This time, the dog had more fun chasing it than the cats. However, after just under 15 minutes of use, it stopped working entirely! Even though I had used brand new batteries in the mouse and the controller when I first got it (a day ago), I replaced all 5 batteries. It does NOT work at all. Nothing happened to it. It did not fall, it didn't' crash, it was not damaged in any way, it simply stopped working altogether in the blink of an eye. And that's a darn shame because my cat AND dog had fun with it. Due to the fact that it stopped working entirely after just under 30 minutes of total use since we got it, and the fact we did nothing to break it/make it stop working, I've changed my rating/review of this item. I cannot recommend an item that stops working out of the blue as this did. For the minutes that it did work, my pets loved it. And we loved watching them have fun.

When you start you'll roll all 9 dice. You must keep at least one, but can reroll all the others, and you continue to reroll until you've set aside all 9 dice at which point you score the dice.

text_fidelity_a:
UBTECH JIMU Robot Builderbots Kit - App Enabled Stem Learning Robotic Building Block Kit (2017) This UBTECH JIMU ROBOT-BUILDERBOTS KIT (Interactive Building Block System (357 Piece)) is so beautifully packaged, you’d almost think it was a smartphone or an Apple product. It comes in a heavy-duty, magnetic-closure box that opens like a book. Inside, the main controller, connectors and fasteners are packed in colorful paper boxes that nest perfectly in the big outer box. Is such a lovely unboxing experience wasted on a kid’s toy?

This kit will make either a “Grabberbot” or a “Digbot”. I say “either”, because the building components are extremely hard to take apart--you are NOT going to want to try a rebuild of either completed robot. Some (but not all) of the components are similar to LEGO Technic elements, but they’re smaller and definitely NOT compatible with LEGO.

In an afternoon (about 4 hours), I built the Grabberbot, which I like a lot. Using the Jimu app (iOS or Android), it’s easy to drive, very responsive, and actually picks things up. Grabberbot has a cool, multicolored LED light (you can program custom colors), and he has a voice cube with a large repertoire of sounds (also programmable).

Grabberbot is controlled with Bluetooth--pairing is easy, once he’s turned on or plugged into a power source. He does NOT have a separate controller, so you must have a tablet or a smartphone to make him work. (I use an iPad Mini.) It’s a good idea to charge the controller cube before you start building--it takes an hour or so. You do NOT want to spend an afternoon building a robot, and then have to wait for the battery to charge before you can play with it!

You can’t build the Grabberbot without a tablet or smartphone--you have to download the app to get the building instructions. (This is a pet peeve of mine; I believe that the instructions for building toys belong in the box.) However, in defense of the download-only instructions, they are presented in 3D! If you’re unsure about a particular step, you can rotate the model 360 degrees and look at it from every angle until you’re sure that you’ve got it right.

Grabberbot is more difficult to build than a motorized LEGO set. There are three reasons for this: (1) the instructions don’t always show the elements recognizably or exactly the way they go together (e.g., the sensor box has fewer connector holes than the one shown in the instructions); (2) the instructions don’t always start at the easiest place for the next step in the assembly; and (3) the components click together so firmly, you need pliers to separate some of them if you make a mistake.

Sadly, the color-changing LED light needs to be programmed if you want it to do more than flash colored lights for a few seconds when Grabberbot is first turned on. I did very little with the programming portion of the app, which requires you to identify which of the four servo motors you want to give instructions to (they are numbered), to choose commands for the motor(s), and to name and record the resulting
action. Programming doesn’t seem to be hard, but it does take some study and practice.

There is a charger with an AC adapter included. The red light on the controller box changes to green when the battery is fully charged. A firmware update starts automatically when you first connect the Grabberbot; it takes only a few minutes.
text_fidelity_b: UBTECH JIMU Robot Builderbots Kit - App Enabled Stem Learning Robotic Building Block Kit (2017)

As most are familiar with the game Jenga, this is essentially played the same way - pull a block from the stack and place it on top. If your block causes the tower to tumble, you lose. The primary difference is the blocks are SUPERSIZED, measuring 7.1”(long) X 2.3”(wide) X 1.4”(tall). The blocks are the perfect size for little hands and kids get the hang of the game quickly and enjoy seeing the tower grow and eventually topple.

Something we do is let the winner of each game write their name, or a short message on a block - it makes it fun to look back and remember the fun we have had during previews games.

In addition there is a white board with a dry erase marker for listing the rules you’ve set for the numbered blocks. text_fidelity_a:
Pathfinder Adventure Card Game: Wrath of the Righteous Base Set We hold a monthly “Game Night” at our house and felt this was the perfect opportunity to introduce the Pathfinder Card game to our friends. Unfortunately, it took at least two hours to explain the rules of the game and our crowd is mostly people over 40, so keeping track of each character’s journey, remembering what powers they do or do not have, and explaining strategy was somewhat difficult, especially as everyone was a first time player. I think this game is best suited to a younger crowd (under 40) but it’s still fun for those who really stick with it.

A few of us played Dungeons & Dragons years ago, so this playing this felt very familiar. Every player is given the opportunity to "customize" their game play, in that they can choose to be a particular character. The characters are individually possessed of different powers, spells, weapons, and capabilities. You choose a specific character and a “scenerio” (a.k.a storyline) and draw cards that determine the path of your journey. Your objective is to maximize your advantage, using the cards and dice to advance or retreat. The objective, of course, is to win the game by overcoming monsters and capturing the bad guys for points. It’s like a video game in that they are different levels and you can move on to different stages. The game shifts scenes as you advance, so it feels like a continual maze. The game can technically go on forever as the company encourages you to buy “expansion sets” that give you additional cards and new adventures to go on.

Two people in our group are big science fiction and fantasy buffs, and they absolutely loved it. For the rest of us, it was challenging, and after playing this for two hours, a little tedious, since it requires so much thinking. This is not a game to be played when you’ve had a few cocktails! But for devoted game geeks, I can see this being a big hit.
text_fidelity_b: Pathfinder Adventure Card Game: Wrath of the Righteous Base Set

text_fidelity_a:
Thomas & Friends Wood, Animal Park Set We have almost the entire Thomas and friends Fisher-Price wood set of the new type of connectors, and we do not have any of the old style tracks from any brands. Overall the new tracks stay together very well and are easy to put together, but in all honesty my three-year-old sometimes has to bring these new style wood tracks to me to get them apart, which she never has to do with the tiny set of traditional tracks that grandma has at her house. What is nice is that you can attach the tracks from either direction, since both sides connect identically.

We have the busy island set, the farm set, cranky at the docks, the train station, and the huge Tidwell sheds station. All of these sets fit together beautifully and provide a lot of different play options for the kids. However, the main complaint I have had is that most of these sets have not come with enough tracks. Even the huge sets, come with just enough tracks to barely get it together if you are very careful and mindful with how you put things together.

The main advantage of a set like this animal park one, is that you get a whole lot of tracks and every piece in it can be used to connect all of the big and exciting things in those huge sets. My daughter also really loved the simplicity of this set, that she doesn't really have to think too hard about how it goes together, she can just wind and turn and connect things up without too much planning ahead.

Overall this set adds to the larger Thomas sets really nicely and is a great way of introducing a little more interest and a lot more tracks into the busy island set or another one of the bigger sets.
text_fidelity_b: Thomas & Friends Wood, Animal Park Set

text_fidelity_a:
Schleich Portable Barn with Accessories The Schleich barn is made of wood and is of extremely high quality except for a problem with the clips and pieces of wood that hold the barn roof together.

The barn opens into two separate unattached halves that slide together at right angles like a puzzle. There are latches on either short side of the barn that can be unlatched to display each half. The barn can be left open or closed. When closed it is easy to carry. A cow, chicken, donkey, lamb, hay bale, basket, red and green vegetables, and a pitch fork and broom are the accessories included. The barn doors on the long side of the barn open in both front and back. The color is vibrant and the farm animals are very realistic.

The only negative I found is that the entire barn is held together with clips that come apart. The clips are not its strongest point. The four clips on either side of the barn roof on mine would not hold up the roof and the boards keep falling off. I tried for over 30 minutes to get two of the clips seated correctly but neither side would snap in place. My boyfriend also looked at this barn and he could not get the clips to seat firmly in place either. He did say, however, that this is a well-made toy. According to the side of the box below the Germany label, it says this is made in Slovakia.

The clips and vegetable pieces that come with the barn can present a choking hazard to a small child. If the child is of that age where items are frequently "tasted," then I recommend adult supervision while the child is playing with this barn. The box indicates that this is not for children under 3 years of age and does state that the small parts present a choking hazard. This is typical of many toys with small parts, however.

Other than this, I got this for my friend's son to play with and he's going to love it. However, he'll have to play with the two roof slats off since they will fall off in its current condition. If the unit I received did not have this problem, I would have rated this 5 stars. Since mine does have this problem, I'm rating it 3. Had I purchased this unit and not received it for review, I would have returned it for a replacement. Since the three other reviewers have not complained about this issue, I suspect it is either a new issue introduced in recent manufacturing design or the unit I received is slightly defective. If there are no other recent reviews that complain about the clips and barn roof, then I would consider this a 5-star toy where I was the one exception. Nevertheless, this defect will not detract from my friend's son enjoyment as young children rarely notice those things.
text_fidelity_b: Schleich Portable Barn with Accessories

LEGO DUPLO My First Tow Truck 10918 Educational Tow Truck Toy, Great Gift for Kids Ages 18 Months and up, New 2020 (6 Pieces) Because I love all LEGO building kits for heavy construction equipment (e.g., [[ASIN:B07Y8T4WHC LEGO Mobile Crane]]), I couldn’t resist this cute little LEGO DUPLO MY FIRST TOW TRUCK 10918 (New 2020 (6 Pieces)). It’s absolutely charming, all 6 pieces of it!

I really like the drivers’ windows, with a boy on one side and a girl on the other. It makes this into a truly unisex toy. I love the big blue traffic cone that fits between the drivers’ cabin and the moveable crane for transport. Tow trucks always set out traffic cones, for safety, when they’re readying a tow. The crane itself is fun because it swings up and down freely.

The building instructions are on the outside of the retail box. The toy takes about 30 seconds for an adult to assemble, as the wheels are already attached to the truck base. When the toy is finished, it makes a terrific truck for general play. The wheels turn freely, and the truck feels solid and satisfying when it’s pushed around.

Inside the box is a printed city street layout. The paper is very thin, so this won’t last long unless it’s glued to some sort of heavier backing. However the street layout fits the assembled tow truck, and is a nice detail.

Note that this is a LEGO duplo model, intended for very young children. The pieces are much larger than standard LEGO pieces. They are compatible with other duplo building sets, but NOT with standard LEGO elements.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO DUPLO My First Tow Truck 10918 Educational Tow Truck Toy, Great Gift for Kids Ages 18 Months and up, New 2020 (6 Pieces)

The first impression of the playset inside the packaging is that it's very cute and attractive. The camper itself is not as durable as I had hoped. This will not stand up to rough play. I would not at all advise this to be accessible to toddlers or careless children because if one tried to use it as a seat or step-stool, it would break easily. The wheels are held in place with a metal rod, this would be a safety hazard if it came out of place. The many small accessories are also not appropriate for very small children as they could pose a choking hazard. There is not enough leg room in the two front seats for the doll's legs, they must be bent to the side or the doll has to sit sideways. Not all of the doors are well-molded to close completely. Some stickers are included, which is nice as one side of the camper already is decorated with stickers, leaving the opposite side blank. Several packets of accessories are included so the dolls can use props for various activities such as cooking, lounging and even showering. The small accessories are the best point of this playset.

I personally do not find this camper set to be a good value at it's current price point. There are too many issues that will lead to frustration in play. Primarily, the type of plastic material used to mold the camper is prone to failure as it's not at all durable. The play patterns of most small children will prove to be the source of frustration or failure of the toy. This type of plastic is prone to shattering and can produce sharp edges if broken. For many children, this will be a short-lived disposable toy. This would be most ideal for children that play gently and are able to keep small toys well organized and enjoy playing with fashion dolls. The camper itself measures about 22" long, 11" wide and 9 1/2" tall. This will need a significant amount of storage space, and would not easily withstand being stored stacked with other toys in a toybox. This would be best 'parked' under a bed, in a closet or on a shelf between play sessions to avoid a tripping hazard. Mega Bloks Call of Duty Desert Tank Building Set Ok first let me say, we are a "it's Lego or its crap" family. My kids evangelize on the evils of Megablocks and other brands they consider knock offs. But this is such a well engineered and detailed set that my fifteen year old wasn't even grudging when he said, this is a really good set.

And he's right, the detail on this set is super impressive. My son loves it for what seems like very authentic design from a war historian rather than a gamer, so maybe a fan of COD would like it even more.

This is a very challenging build, filled with small parts and unlike Lego that pre bags parts so you can open a single bag to do the first couple pages of instructions, mega blocks has you open 80% of the bags for the first few pages. You end up with an impressive pile of pieces out there. Also unlike Lego, mega blocks will create molded pieces specific to a model so realism can be pushed farther than Lego does. In this set, the body is filled with parts that are not just molded to shape but also in color to seem camouflaged or dirty from use. This truly lends a wonderful realism to the model. We also appreciated that markings are screen printed onto pieces rather than using stickers. Kudos for doing that it makes it feel like a quality set.

I do notice a bit more brittleness in the blocks and brick for brick the quality does not seem to match lego, but I can do little but rave over this set. It is beautiful, it took my son and I working together to get this done in several hours. And once done, this is a beautiful set for display.

Well done Mega Block, you are doing what I thought was impossible, you are winning us over from Lego.

*** additional

My son wanted me to mention that the instructions were hard, I would use challenging. But one thing I did forget, I am partially colorblind and often found it hard to distinguish colors in the instructions if it was not daylight.
text_fidelity_b: Mega Bloks Call of Duty Desert Tank Building Set

My First Sewing Kit by Alex Crafts, Perfect for Beginners, Arts and Crafts Colorful and Fun Sewing Projects to Learn the Basic Skills of Sewing (Ages 7+) This possibly isn't the best starter kit for a child who has never sewn before. The instructions aren't that good. If the child has done any other sewing, or has anyone who can help (can be another kid) then this will provide a great deal of practice, which is where this really shines.

There are quite a few projects here. There is a draw string bag, a stuffed cat, a stuffed dog, a stuffed elephant, and a book cover with pencil holder wrapper.

For supplies, it has everything - scissor, tape measure, pins, pin cushion, button, even some extra stuff, like pop poms, that you won't need for any of the projects. There definitely is not even close to enough stuffing. It did not quite fill the cat, which is the first, and smallest, of the stuffed animal projects. You'll want to pick up something like [[ASIN:B000YZ7G44 Fairfield Poly-Fil Premium Polyester Fiber, White, 1 Bag, 12-Ounce]]. Any fiberfill will do, but this is a good one, similar to what is in the kit. While on the topic of stuffing, a double pointed knitting needle, or better http://www.amazon.com/Little-Foot-That-Purple-Thang-/dp/B001ELBCFG/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1464647654&sr=8-1&keywords=purple+thang will help get the stuffing into the tight areas, like the tails. Both the fiberfill and the thang will be useful items in a variety of sewing projects.

For the embroidery floss, it says to cut the skein on one side to make lengths. That works, no issue, but it might be better to make a little yarn butterfly (really simple; instructions are online) so that you can pull the length you need for each section and the leftovers, and there will be plenty, can be used to make friendship bracelets. There is an excess of embroidery floss here.

text_fidelity_a:
Arm & Hammer Baking Soda Color Creations, Island Green, 1 Lb I love to have the ability to bring out different ingredients to make either natural body care, or crafts. Having colored baking soda seemed like a great idea, but there is a problem..

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This is a pound of baking soda which is colored up to what I would call a shamrock green. it is housed in a thin plastic bag which is supposed to be able to be cut and reseal. The green color itself is not overbearing. There is a recipe for clay on the package along with tips on how to use this.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
This would have been a more pleasant experience, but the plastic bag this comes in is very fragile. This came to me exuding green powder all over me and the mail delivery person. Upon examination, the bag itself is very easily punctured and cracked. That means that storing the baking soda back in the bag is a BAD idea. If you drop it, it will break.

As for what we made, I did a very small batch of bath bomb and it was fun. I used the white swirled with the green and it worked out okay. The green did not stain the tub badly and seemed to rinse out pretty well. As for making baking soda clay ornaments, I tried a sample of that and it was not bad either- the green is great to use in Christmas decorations from the clay/dough.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a pretty good idea, but the packaging is awful. Even if it does not come broken, it is hard to reseal due to the soda getting in the plastic reseal slide. I would like it better if it came in a tub- with a window that is clear- somewhat bendable and not fragile.

MY RATING
THREE STARS. This needs to come in a tub that has a bit of resilience to it and is see through too. It just is not practical to use or ship with such fragile plastic packaging. The product itself is okay, and worth three stars, but the way they market it needs to be better.
text_fidelity_b: Arm & Hammer Baking Soda Color Creations, Island Green, 1 Lb

ENJBRICK Harry Castle Potter Toy Building Set,Compatible with Lego Idea Building Blocks Kit for Kids and Adults 521pcs This set consists of thirteen #1 bags for Weasley's Wizarding Wheezes (the purple and orange building), eight #2 bags for Flourish and Blotts (the green and brown building), one bag of plates, instructions, and a small sticker sheet.

The bags are not numbered individually. Trust me, open all the bags for a building. So all #1 bags or all #2 bags. You’ll need a lot of space for the pieces, but it’s less frustrating in the long run. Steps require pieces from every bag as you go. Finding the pieces for each step took the longest part of this build.

The instructions are mostly clear*, but the build experience itself is frustrating. Some pieces stay together and some do not. I spent so much time rebuilding because a section would break when I put new pieces on. For example, the window section for WWW, I had to test window pieces to see which would stay together and then stay on the building. For the upper window section, where the arms come out, I had to redo that three or four times, carefully holding the windows together.

*Step 64 has the wrong pieces, there is a sheet to show the proper pieces.

The buildings are delicate. On my Flourish and Blotts building, the bottom barely stays together, so I can’t take it off the base. The buildings are hollow inside, so you can hide items. The F&B building has a tray inside, and the WWW building has a rod to use to pop the tray out. If I popped the tray out, I’d have to put the F&B building back together. I don’t care for the hiding space, I’d prefer buildings that were more stable, especially if they’re supposed to be bookends.

Some of the stickers go over multiple pieces, one sticker on 2 or 3 pieces. The Dark Mark sticker is misspelled: DRRK MRRK.

Overall, the finished set looks good, but getting to that finished set was a somewhat frustrating experience.

text_fidelity_a:
Kid Galaxy RC Off Road Car. Claw Climber Tiger 4x4 Remote Control Vehicle, 2.4 GHz Wow! My toddler had been in a terrible mood all day, the sort of no good mood in which nothing satisfies and none of the toys or projects he was working on seem to come out right. Even a nap didn't cure it, but I'll tell you what did: this vehicle arriving in the mail. The presentation is awesome. You can see the face of the vehicle and the cool claws on the tires right from the get-go, and he immediately got excited. Though he is totally into trucks, construction vehicles, and things that go of all kinds, this got a higher level of excitement out of him because of how it was personified – it looks a little like Bowser from Super Mario Brothers, or has that same kind of appeal.

But, for a not quite three-year-old in a terrible mood, would he be able to work it? Though I've tested about 15 RC vehicles in the last year trying to find just the right one that he will be able to enjoy controlling, without going too fast, too slow, bottoming out on small obstacles, tipping over when driven over slopes, or being generally too complicated to run in some respect, only a few have passed the "I can do it myself" test. This is one of them.

The remote control is simple to understand and use, fits in small hands, and is lightweight and chunky to hold. Perfect for a toddler. There also isn't any pokey wire or metal antennae sticking out. I always wonder how companies justify giving that to a kid, given that they're going to be sprinting across the lawn not looking where they are going and liable to poke somebody's eye out, or their own if they fall.

I also really liked the speed level of this. I would've been happy if it were also a little slower to allow for better reaction time, but the speed was fast enough to be fun but not so fast that it's hard to control with childlike reflexes.

But the very best thing about it is those clawlike tires and the suspension. The claws are made of a softer rubberized plastic material, and the claws flap out with the centrifugal force of the tires movements, and retract in as needed. It's not something you can really control, they just do it themselves. Mine seem to have an error where one of the tires has the claws stuck inside for the most part and trying to pull them out on my own didn't work that well, they just retracted again and stayed retracted as soon as I started the vehicle again. No matter, it almost seems to help the car have better traction to have one back wheel that is essentially without claws.

The claws grip onto pretty much any surface, carpet, blankets, toys, rocks, lawn and woodchips, and thrust them out of the way so the car can off-road just about anywhere. We, perhaps unwisely, began our testing in the living room, where it climbed over a wide array of baby and toddler toys, turning upside down, then catching on a blanket and turning itself right back up before getting stuck in a ridiculously large mashup of garbage truck and Duplo bricks. It was exciting, impressive how it righted itself and went over such a wide variety of huge objects, and loads and loads of fun.

I also love the high suspension. Many other trucks, even ones with big monster tires such as from John Deere, ruin things by having a small plastic box on the underside of the vehicle which hangs downward and makes the vehicles bottom out on anything it hits. I don't know why this is such a "thing", but at least half of the RC vehicles we've gotten have this exact problem, even the off-road ones. This little truck does not suffer from that issue, and thus was able to go through a wide variety of terrains, and nothing seemed to stop it. It was going sideways on a pile of landscape trimmings, went upside down, righted itself, clawed its way all the way through the backyard and house with no issues.

The one complaint I have is not really a complaint, just a minor caution. It looks as though there is not really any way for sand and dirt and mud to work itself out of the holes in the tires were it to get truly filthy. We solve this problem by not taking it to the sand dunes or running it through sand or mud. We brought it to the playground that has woodchips and lawn, in the backyard that has woodchips and lawn, and discouraged our toddler from using it in the dusty vegetable beds in the backyard. No problem. However, if your vision is to bring it someplace truly dirty, I have no idea what the longevity would be and how nice the vehicle would look and work after prolonged running through such materials. It is off-road, but not necessarily all-terrain.

Overall, this is probably my favorite RC vehicle we've gotten yet. It is just so much fun, has great personality and really made an impression on our toddler, is easy to control, and doesn't have many of the issues that previous RC vehicles have suffered from. A thoughtfully designed toy all around, and fun for the whole family. I definitely don't feel too old for this, and my almost 3-year-old toddler isn't too young, so that's quite a range.
text_fidelity_b: Kid Galaxy RC Off Road Car. Claw Climber Tiger 4x4 Remote Control Vehicle, 2.4 GHz

text_fidelity_a:
4DV2 Foldable Mini Drone with 720P Camera for Kids,2.4G FPV Video,Nano Portable Pocket RC Quadcopter Beginners Toys,3D Flip,Altitude Hold,Headless Mode,Trajectory Flight,3D Flips,3 Battery [[VIDEOID:8a35051fba3b622e613e552275a81a53]] This is a great starter drone, in theory. I have flown many of these and my son wanted to try one to get started with. He picked it up really quickly and together we were able to fly it around the house indoors without hitting anything. The camera is gimmicky at best, but for the price I'd say get it for the drone flight fun and forget the camera.
UNTIL... within 2 days of owning it, something seemed to go wrong with the height sensor (barometer?), and it not only wouldn't hold the correct height like it did the day before, but suddenly it shot straight UP. No pressing down on the joystick seems to change anything. Its as if the unit felt like it was falling and needed to compensate by flying more aggressively upwards. It hit the ceiling, and we promptly hit the kill switch. I took a look at it, pulled off the propellers to look, and tried again. Same thing - it shot straight UP. Hit the ceiling. I tried cleaning any hair/debris from the blades and again- straight up until it hit. But this time, it started making a funny noise. Upon closer inspection I found one of the pins that the propeller sits on has been bent. I don't know if this was caused by it going straight up or if it caused it, but the drone has been grounded for now. You can see in the attached video how when that pin is spun, it tilts forward and back, rather that the other pins which spin in place.
It is possibly that I just got a dud and others would love this, I wouldn't mind trying it again and seeing if I have a different outcome. It did work really well for the first 2 days, and I really like that it not only has a replaceable battery but comes with 2 additional batteries as well! Flight times are usually small on these things so having many extra batteries ready to go is useful. If it hadn't gone nuts and shot upwards everytime, I'd give this thing 5 stars. I'm going to see what I can about sourcing a replacement or additional unit and come back to update this review if it turns out I had a lemon.
text_fidelity_b: 4DV2 Foldable Mini Drone with 720P Camera for Kids,2.4G FPV Video,Nano Portable Pocket RC Quadcopter Beginners Toys,3D Flip,Altitude Hold,Headless Mode,Trajectory Flight,3D Flips,3 Battery

Monster High Travel Scaris Scooter Vehicle Monster High toys and accessories are a huge hit with their fan base and the Travel Scaris Convertible vehicle is bound to be a big hit with kids who love Monster High. It is a stylish and attractive toy vehicle with a design that sets it apart from the average kid's toy vehicle.

I'm not usually very impressed with toy vehicles because I have seen so many of them and because most of them look very similar. But this toy vehicle grabbed my attention. The cool, eye- catching, all- around design pattern is one that is bound to warrant a second look and both adults and kids alike will find that it easily stands out against other toy vehicles.

Aside from the exterior, this Monster High vehicle does have other features that make it cool. The stylish wheels glide smoothly across a tile floor or a table without any problem and the vehicle seats up to four Monster High dolls. Rather than have all four dolls face forward, this convertible is a two- seat model with a pair of seats that are actually on top of the trunk, where the dolls face backward. Again, it's something unique that you don't find with other toy vehicles.

The Monster High Travel Scaris Vehicle doesn't have any lights or sounds. This may bother some youngsters, but it is better from an adult perspective because it means no batteries to buy and more imagination required. Most kids will not mind anyway- they will find the vehicle so cool and fun that they will not even notice that it doesn't make noise or have any lights. And another advantage is that boys and girls both seem to like this toy. Girls like it because its Monster High and boys like it because, well, it's a vehicle, which is a toy normally associated with boys.

This Monster High vehicle doesn't have opening side doors, and this is one quality that I wish was different because it would not only look cool, but it would also make it easier to place the dolls into the seats. But other than that, this is a fun, nice- looking toy that belongs in the home of every Monster High fan.
text_fidelity_b: Monster High Travel Scaris Scooter Vehicle

text_fidelity_a:
Hygge Games How did You Know That? – Trivia Party Game, White As a lover of board games… Our family members each receive a new addition to the game closet in their stocking every year… With kids off to college- I am constantly looking for new and fun options that don’t take a lot explaining or, learning and can peek their interest, liking them to be a bit competitive yet, can be played with minimal effort- So, a hard combo to find! So, I’m happy to say… “How did You know That-“ falls into this category!!

DID YOU KNOW THAT is easy enough to learn and that’s a perk! Also, a big plus is the fact, it’s easy to explain it to those who have a tendency to not pay attention during rule reading (we all know a few of “those type” people- ha ha..!!) BUT, with an easy concept they’ll be playing like pros in no time.. LOVE the fact, this game can be tweaked and adapted if necessary.. and we always love those! (Anything that allows you to simplify or shorten a game as needed.. is like sprinkles on top!)

Basic idea: one person reads 4 questions in a row off of x1 card. All other players write their 4 answers down… THEN, players will correct answers as revealed for all 4 questions asked. giving x1 pt. per correct answer. If only x1 person gets it right the crowd shouts “how did you know that!” and gets double points. Its that simple..

This is full of Quirky odd questions at various levels of some useful/not trivia! Winner is whoever has most points at the end of game..
Best part is: YOU decide do you play to a certain point level (1st one to 10, 20 wins?) OR, do you give everyone certain amount of cards so, everyone has a turn or two to read questions.. if so then, at the end of all reveals.. they tally up those points received to see who’s the winner! That’s it..!!!

This would make a great game for the dorms- (especially during the time of the pandemic.. these kids have a lot of Shelter in place/quarantine time!) for those old enough, I could see it turning this into a drinking game of sorts (good or, bad?!) it would easily adapt.
Definitely, feel this is geared toward older teens or, adults.. it’s too hard for younger kids. I do feel this has a niché for academics and know it alls! Any with mega time spent learning, reading, gaining random facts off the Internet- it’s a great way to share that trivial academia skills.. Ha! Some things will just be fun facts you picked up thru life, in elementary school or, info. From those who’ve raised you.. tossed with real trivia facts. So, the smartest person doesn’t always win!? Fun for a competitive group with a plethora of knowledge and facts to share!!
Played with our college kids over holiday and it went back to the dorm bc, of its fun factor- with x3 college kids and/or, recent graduates.. we had a ball! I hope this info can help your decision.. feel free to let me know!
text_fidelity_b: Hygge Games How did You Know That? – Trivia Party Game, White

text_fidelity_a:
Munchkin We've only had the game for a few days, but so far we've played it a total of six times, you figure each game is one hour long, so basically we've gotten six hours of fun for the affordable price of under twenty bucks. So, way less than we'd spend if my family went out to see a movie and best of all, we didn't even have to leave the house.

A little bit about the game, it seemed a bit complicated at first.

We followed the directions, give each player four cards each from the two stacks, that part was basic, but we ended up folding and unfolding the game play instructions trying to figure out what to do next.

Basically, each player tries to level up. Levelling up can be achieved in just a few ways, 1. defeating a monster (which you can only do if you have enough levels, which means you may need to, 2. buy a level, by selling magical items or 3. get a level up treasure card.

The game seemed a bit slow at first because each player starts with just one level which is too low to start fighting monsters. But the game picked up when we'd all gotten to level three. The monsters can be defeated by more than one player, so one minute I was sabotaging my son's chances at winning another level, the next we were fighting flying frogs together and sharing in the loot!

The cards themselves give you directions, telling you to add 5 to fight a monster (very useful card to use against your opponents) or that certain magical items can only be used by certain characters; dwarves, elves, etc.

By the time we played a third time, we knew the game well enough to start levelling curses at each other and how to steal each others treasures.

Munchkin has a lot of extender packs, munchkin zombie, munchkin the guild (I just bought this one, yay!) etc. that add to the original game set.

Since we play a lot of games here at home, monopoly, settlers of catan, telepathy, zombie dice, risk, etc. figuring out the basic rules wasn't terribly difficult, but I think looking at a few munchkin blogs could prove helpful (yep, there really are munchkin blogs.)
text_fidelity_b: Munchkin

text_fidelity_a:
Legacy Deluxe Mancala Classic Game with Folding Wooden Game Board and Colored Glass Stones, Family Game for Ages 8 and up Chess has been my favorite board game since I was a child and I have collected chess sets as a hobby over the years. When I selected this one I expected it to be on par with typical portable wooden sets which are usually cheaply made. This one was a pleasant surprise in that it is a step up from most portable wooden sets I have seen and used.

This is a fairly straightforward set. The case is a clamshell design that folds open into the board. There are magnets in the rim of the underside of the board to hold it closed when the set is not in use, ands the manufacturer did a decent job of concealing the contacts (though they are visible if you look for them). The squares on the board are smooth and while the seams between the squares can be felt when you run your hand along the board, the seams are smooth and are less pronounced that what I have seen on some other boards.

The pieces are decently made though are nothing special. They are machine cut pieces and have been smoothed, sanded and varnished. They are weighted nicely and have felt on the bottom to avoid scratching the board. They’re a fairly average design but they look good and are very recognizable.

The main feature of this set is that it is larger than most fold-out boards I have seen and used. While this might not be the best for packing and portability, I really like the size. I am less likely to knock over pieces accidentally and I can see what’s going on a little better.

This is not just a chess set but includes wood chips for playing checkers as well. The chips are small and are nothing of note but they are sufficient.

I really like this chess set and will use it as my main travel set moving forward. I like the size of the board, the feel of the pieces and the overall quality. There are better sets out there but they cost more. There are less expensive sets too, and the chances of finding one that is of the same quality as this one for less is small.
text_fidelity_b: Legacy Deluxe Mancala Classic Game with Folding Wooden Game Board and Colored Glass Stones, Family Game for Ages 8 and up
